name: Speaker invite
description: Invites someone to speak at an event. States the date, the audience and the format in the first message, because a speaker's first three questions are always when, to whom, and how long.
audience: People whose work makes a talk obvious: they have shipped the thing your audience wants to hear about.

variants: {{firstName|Hi}} — I programme an event for {{title|people in your field}} and your work at {{company|your company}} is exactly what the audience keeps asking for. Connecting with an invitation.
Hi {{firstName|there}} — putting together a lineup and would like you on it. Connecting so I can send the detail properly.
Thanks {{firstName|there}}. Specifics: around 200 practitioners, 25-minute talk plus questions, travel covered, and you keep the recording. Would you take the slot?
Detail first, {{firstName|there}}: 200-odd in the room, 25 minutes, expenses covered, recording is yours. Interested in principle?
{{firstName|Hi}} — happy to work around the date, or take a panel instead of a talk if that's easier on your diary.
If a full talk is too much, {{firstName|there}}, a panel seat is thirty minutes of your day and no prep. Either works for us.
I'll close the lineup this week, {{firstName|there}} — no problem if the timing's wrong. I'll ask again for the next one.
Finalising the programme, {{firstName|there}}. If it's a no this time I'll come back for the next edition.
